title: A Vendor Prepayment Exception Denied on Spend Size
scenario_text:
A procurement analyst at Kingsley Logistics must decide whether an annual-prepayment exception can be approved at the team level, given how a similar request was handled earlier this year.

**Decision A (2024-03)**
Vendor 'Aldworth Freight Systems' | annual contract $90K. Requested full annual prepayment instead of the standard quarterly billing. Procurement DECLINED at the team level. Note: 'Prepayment exceptions require Finance approval unless annual spend is at least $150K, in which case Procurement may approve prepayment directly. Aldworth was $90K — below the threshold — and no Finance approval was obtained. Declined.'

**Current request C (2024-10-01)**
Vendor 'Brenton Fleet Services' | annual contract $185K. Requesting full annual prepayment in exchange for a 6% discount. The contract is otherwise standard.

**Prepayment Authority Policy (current, unchanged since 2023-08)**
Standard vendor billing is quarterly. Prepayment exceptions require Finance approval, EXCEPT that when a vendor's annual spend is at least $150K, Procurement may approve annual prepayment directly. This spend-based authority has been in place since August 2023.

**Slack — #procurement**
Buyer: 'We declined a prepayment ask back in March for a similar setup, so we should route Brenton to Finance too.'
Analyst: 'The March one was declined for a reason — let me check Brenton's annual spend against the threshold before we assume Finance has to approve it.'

No one has yet compared Brenton's $185K annual spend to the $150K threshold that changes who can approve.
question: How should the analyst handle Brenton Fleet Services' prepayment request?
choices: Route the prepayment request to Finance for approval, consistent with the March decision on a similar request.

Approve the annual prepayment directly at the Procurement level, because Brenton's $185K annual spend clears the $150K threshold that grants Procurement authority — a path the March vendor never qualified for.
Decline the prepayment request, since prepayment exceptions are not permitted without escalation.
Approve prepayment for only two quarters as a compromise, routing the rest to Finance.
